summary: Mitigate observed Mac Web EMFILE under concurrent session/job polling by raising only the Web process soft descriptor limit and closing event segment directory scans deterministically.

components.owning_subsystem: Existing runtime.launch managed Web service entrypoint and process-local operating-system resource limits; service_control still owns deployment, restart and live identity.
components.disposition: Only after the non-mutating dry-run path, increase the Web child process RLIMIT_NOFILE soft limit to at most 1024 and never above its existing hard limit. Fail-soft when the OS refuses. Do not change system-wide launchd limits, permissions, other services, API, model, Host or tool authority.
evidence: Production Mac launchctl maxfiles soft=256, hard=unlimited; Web PID 16924 had high CPU and intermittent 5-15 second /health timeouts; web.log contained 16 OSError Errno24 Too many open files exceptions associated with session job and escalation reads.
A separate isolated macOS child process successfully changed RLIMIT_NOFILE from (256, unlimited) to (1024, unlimited); no production process was modified.
Focused runtime and event-log tests 20 plus 39 passed; Ruff passed. Independent Reviewer, original complete R9, remote CI, protected merge and managed deployment remain required.
components.verification_level: Isolated code candidate and focused tests only; no production activation or full R9 claim until exact final SHA is frozen.
components.model_evidence_veto_recovery_exit: No model evidence, veto, approval, replay or execution authority is introduced. The OS limit is a process-local soft resource ceiling only; hard cap, identity checks and managed deployment remain unchanged. On setrlimit error, preserve current startup behavior and report a warning.
components.rollback_route: Revert the bounded launch helper and its tests through protected main, then use existing managed service control only after active Web and Learning runs drain; retain unrelated PR #109 and other Goals.

components.owning_subsystem: Existing EventStore segment path enumeration; the same sorted segment list and last_seq semantics remain authoritative.
components.disposition: Use os.scandir as a context manager in active/all segment enumeration to release directory descriptors even if entry inspection or sorting raises. Preserve segment order, errors, event replay, append locking and storage layout.
evidence: Production EMFILE trace includes event_log/store.py _all_segment_paths and last_seq during jobs polling.
New tests inject OSError from an entry for both scan methods and assert deterministic iterator closure; existing event-log regression suite passes.
components.verification_level: Targeted tests passed; independent Reviewer, full R9, final SHA CI and production validation pending.
components.model_evidence_veto_recovery_exit: No model or Host control. The context manager changes only descriptor lifetime, not error propagation or durable event facts. Existing EventStore recovery and rollback behavior is retained.
components.rollback_route: Revert the two with-scandir wrappers if regression is detected, preserving all event log data and concurrent Goal state.
